ingredients_json: ["180 g strawberries, fresh, sliced", "320 g strawberries, frozen, unsweetened", "60 g maple syrup", "20 g cornstarch", "250 g Greek yogurt, low-fat", "250 ml oat milk, unsweetened", "1 piece lemon, zest and juice", "120 g rolled oats", "60 g whole wheat flour", "40 g unsalted butter", "1 piece egg, raw", "1 g vanilla extract", "2 g salt", "10 g ground almonds"]
instructions:
Heat the oven to 180°C. In a bowl, mix the oats, whole wheat flour, ground almonds, and salt, then rub in the butter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Beat the egg with the vanilla, stir it into the crumb mixture, and press the dough into a greased 20–22 cm pie dish. Bake the crust for 12–15 minutes until lightly golden, then let it cool.

Meanwhile, thaw the frozen strawberries and place them in a saucepan with the maple syrup and lemon juice. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. In a small cup, mix the cornstarch with 60 ml of the oat milk until smooth, then pour it into the simmering berries while whisking. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the filling thickens and turns glossy, then fold in the fresh sliced strawberries and lemon zest. Let the berry filling cool to room temperature.

For the cream, whisk the Greek yogurt with the remaining oat milk until smooth and creamy. Spread the yogurt cream over the cooled crust, then spoon the strawberry filling on top. Chill the pie for at least 4 hours, until set. Slice and serve cold for the cleanest, best-tasting texture.

title: Light Vanilla Strawberry Shortcakes with Greek Yogurt Cream
ingredients_json: ["180 g strawberries, fresh", "20 g sugar, granulated", "450 g Greek yogurt, plain, nonfat", "2 tbsp lemon juice, fresh", "300 g flour, whole wheat", "40 g sugar, granulated", "10 g baking powder", "2 g salt, fine", "120 ml milk, low-fat (1–2%)", "80 g butter, unsalted", "2 piece egg, whole, raw", "5 ml vanilla extract", "30 g rolled oats"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with parchment. Hull the strawberries and slice them, then toss with 20 g sugar and 2 tbsp lemon juice; let them sit while you make the shortcakes so they release juices. In a bowl, mix the whole wheat flour, 40 g sugar, baking powder, salt, and rolled oats. In another bowl, whisk the eggs with the milk and vanilla extract, then melt the butter and stir it in. Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix just until a thick dough forms; avoid overmixing so the shortcakes stay tender. Spoon the dough into 8 small rounds on the tray and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch. Cool the shortcakes for 5 minutes, then split them and assemble with a generous layer of Greek yogurt cream and macerated strawberries. Serve soon for the best contrast between fluffy cake and juicy berries.

title: Whole-Grain Strawberry Shortcakes with Greek Yogurt Cream
ingredients_json: ["250 g strawberries, fresh", "30 g honey", "300 g Greek yogurt, nonfat", "30 g powdered sugar", "1 g vanilla extract", "200 g whole-wheat flour", "15 g baking powder", "5 g fine salt", "80 g unsalted butter, cold", "60 g rolled oats", "120 ml milk, low-fat (1-2%)", "1 piece egg, raw", "10 g lemon juice, fresh"]
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with parchment. Slice the strawberries and toss them with the honey and lemon juice in a bowl. Let them sit for 10 minutes so they release juices. In a large bowl, combine the whole-wheat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, and salt. Cut the cold butter into small pieces and rub it into the dry ingredients until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg with the low-fat milk and vanilla extract, then pour into the dry mixture and stir just until a thick dough forms. Scoop the dough into 8 small rounds onto the tray, spacing them apart, and bake for 12–15 minutes until golden and springy to the touch. Meanwhile, mix the nonfat Greek yogurt with the powdered sugar until smooth. Let the shortcakes cool for 10 minutes, then split them, spoon on the strawberry mixture (including some of the juice), and finish with the yogurt cream.

title: Light Strawberry Shortcakes with Greek Yogurt Shortcake Biscuits
ingredients_json: ["300 g strawberries, fresh", "30 g sugar, granulated", "500 g plain low-fat Greek yogurt", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "320 g whole wheat flour", "40 g oat flour", "12 g baking powder", "6 g fine salt", "80 g light butter, unsalted", "140 ml milk, semi-skimmed", "1 piece egg", "25 g powdered erythritol"]
instructions: Hull and slice the strawberries. Simmer them with the granulated sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until the juices thicken slightly and the berries are glossy. Let the mixture cool to room temperature. For the shortcake, preheat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray. In a bowl, whisk together whole wheat flour, oat flour, baking powder, and fine salt. Rub the light butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Whisk the egg with the milk and vanilla, then stir into the flour mixture until a soft dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface, pat it to about 2 cm thick, and cut into 8 small rounds. Bake for 12–15 minutes until risen and lightly golden on top. Cool the biscuits briefly. Whisk the Greek yogurt with the powdered erythritol. Split the warm biscuits, spoon over yogurt, and finish with the strawberry topping. Serve promptly for the best texture.

title: Light Strawberry Shortcakes with Greek Yogurt Biscuits and Vanilla
ingredients_json: ["250 g strawberries, fresh", "15 g honey", "250 g low-fat Greek yogurt, plain", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "200 g all-purpose wheat flour", "30 g whole-wheat flour", "50 g rolled oats", "10 g baking powder", "2 g fine salt", "60 g unsalted butter", "80 ml semi-skimmed milk", "10 ml lemon juice", "1 large egg"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with parchment paper. Hull and slice the strawberries, then toss them in a bowl with the honey and lemon juice. Let them sit for 10 minutes so they release some juice. In another bowl, whisk the all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, oats, baking powder, and salt. Add the butter and rub it into the dry ingredients until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Beat the egg with the milk and vanilla, then stir into the dry mixture just until a thick dough forms. Scoop 8 mounds onto the tray and gently flatten them. Bake for 12–15 minutes until the shortcakes are golden and spring back when lightly pressed. While they bake, stir the Greek yogurt until smooth. Let the shortcakes cool for 5 minutes, then split them, spoon over the strawberries with a little syrup, and finish with a generous dollop of yogurt.

title: Whole-Grain Strawberry Shortcakes with Greek Yogurt Cream
ingredients_json: ["220 g strawberries, fresh", "30 g honey", "1 tbsp lemon juice", "150 g plain Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "250 g whole wheat flour", "30 g oats, rolled", "40 g almond flour", "10 g baking powder", "2 g fine salt", "60 g unsalted butter", "30 g maple syrup", "1 piece egg, raw", "2 dl milk, low-fat", "5 g vanilla extract"]
instructions: Hull and slice the strawberries, then combine them in a bowl with the honey and lemon juice. Let them sit for 15 minutes so they release their juices. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with parchment. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, almond flour, baking powder, and salt. In another bowl, whisk the egg, milk, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and melted butter, then pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until you have a thick, slightly sticky dough. Divide the dough into 8 mounds on the tray and lightly flatten them. Bake for 12–15 minutes, until the shortcakes are golden and spring back when touched. While they cool, stir the Greek yogurt until smooth; if you prefer it sweeter, fold in a spoon of the strawberry syrup from the bowl. Split the shortcakes, spoon over the strawberries and syrup, add a generous dollop of yogurt cream, and serve right away.

title: Whole Wheat Vanilla Almond Sugar Cookies with Yogurt Glaze
ingredients_json: ["150 g whole wheat pastry flour", "80 g rolled oats, finely ground", "90 g unsalted butter, softened", "100 g plain Greek yogurt, 2%", "70 g light brown sugar", "1 piece egg, raw", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "2 g baking powder", "2 g fine salt", "40 g almonds, finely chopped", "80 g powdered sugar", "15 ml lemon juice"]
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C. Line two baking trays with baking paper. In a bowl, rub the softened butter together with the light brown sugar until creamy. Beat in the egg, then mix in the Greek yogurt and vanilla extract. In a second bowl, combine the whole wheat pastry flour, ground oats, baking powder, and fine salt. Add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and mix until a soft dough forms. Fold in the chopped almonds. Roll the dough to about 1 cm thickness on a lightly floured surface and cut out cookies with a cookie cutter. Place cookies on the trays with a little space between them. Bake for 9–11 minutes, until the edges are set and lightly golden but the centers still look tender. Cool the cookies on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. To make the glaze, stir powdered sugar with lemon juice until smooth and thick enough to drizzle; spoon or lightly brush over the cooled cookies, then let set for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Whole-Grain Vanilla Sugar Cookies with Greek Yogurt Glaze
ingredients_json: ["180 g whole wheat pastry flour", "40 g rolled oats, finely ground", "110 g Greek yogurt, plain, 2%", "90 g unsalted butter, softened", "70 g light brown sugar", "1 piece egg, raw", "1 g baking powder", "2 g vanilla extract", "3 g salt", "30 ml milk, 2%", "60 g powdered sugar", "10 g lemon juice, fresh"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C and line two baking trays with baking paper. In a large bowl, mix the whole wheat pastry flour, finely ground oats, baking powder, and salt. In another bowl, cream the softened butter with the light brown sugar until it looks paler and fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract, then stir in the Greek yogurt until smooth. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix just until a soft dough forms; if it feels too dry, add the milk a little at a time. Roll the dough to about 6 mm thick on a lightly floured surface and cut into cookie shapes. Place the cookies on the trays and bake for 9–11 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden and the centers still look set. Cool the cookies on the tray for 5 minutes before transferring to a rack to cool completely. For the glaze, whisk powdered sugar with lemon juice and a small spoon of warm water (or a few drops of milk) until pourable, then drizzle over the cooled cookies and let set for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Whole-Wheat Vanilla Sugar Cookies with Greek Yogurt Glaze
ingredients_json: ["160 g whole wheat flour", "40 g all-purpose flour", "80 g unsalted butter, cold", "150 g Greek yogurt, plain 2%", "120 g light brown sugar", "1 piece egg, raw", "5 g baking powder", "2 g fine salt", "10 g vanilla extract", "60 g powdered sugar", "15 ml lemon juice"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C and line two baking trays with parchment paper. In a bowl, cream the cold unsalted butter with the light brown sugar until the mixture looks lighter and slightly fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract, then mix in the Greek yogurt until smooth. In a separate bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and fine salt, then add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and stir just until a soft dough forms. If the dough feels very sticky, refrigerate it for 10–15 minutes so it’s easier to roll. Roll the dough to about 5 mm thick and cut out cookie shapes, then place them on the trays with a little space between each. Bake for 9–11 minutes, until the edges are lightly golden and the centers look set but not browned. Cool the cookies on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. For the glaze, whisk the powdered sugar with the lemon juice until smooth and drizzle or spread thinly over the cooled cookies.

title: Whole-Grain Oat Sugar Cookies with Vanilla Bean and Greek Yogurt
ingredients_json: ["170 g rolled oats, finely ground", "120 g whole wheat flour", "100 g unsalted butter, softened", "80 g light brown sugar", "1 piece egg, raw", "100 g plain Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "1 tbsp milk, 1.5% fat", "1 tbsp vanilla extract", "5 g baking powder", "2 g fine sea salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with parchment paper. In a bowl, mix the ground oats, whole wheat flour, baking powder, and sea salt. In a separate bowl, cream the softened butter with the light brown sugar until smooth and lighter in color. Beat in the egg, then mix in the Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, and milk until you have a thick, cohesive dough. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and stir just until no dry flour remains, being careful not to overmix. Roll the dough between two sheets of parchment to about 5 mm thickness, then cut out cookie shapes and place them on the tray with a little spacing. Bake for 9–11 minutes, until the edges look set and lightly golden but the centers still feel slightly soft. Let the cookies cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely before serving.

title: Creamy Roasted Sweet Potato Pie with Cinnamon and Vanilla
ingredients_json: ["450 g sweet potato, raw", "250 g Greek yogurt, plain, 2% fat", "2 large eggs", "80 g honey", "60 g whole wheat flour", "60 g unsalted butter", "1 tbsp brown sugar", "1 tsp ground cinnamon", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "0.5 tsp ground ginger", "0.25 tsp fine salt", "1 tbsp milk, semi-skimmed"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C. Peel and cube the sweet potatoes, then spread them on a baking tray and roast for 25–30 minutes until very soft. Let them cool slightly, then mash until smooth. In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the honey, vanilla extract, cinnamon, ginger, and salt. Melt the butter, cool it for 2 minutes, and whisk it in. Fold in the Greek yogurt and the mashed sweet potatoes. Stir in the whole wheat flour until the mixture is smooth and cohesive. Grease a 20–22 cm pie dish, pour in the filling, and tap the dish gently on the counter to remove air bubbles. Bake for 35–45 minutes, until the edges look set and the center has a slight wobble like set custard. Cool for at least 1 hour before slicing so the pie firms up. If you want a glossy top, brush the surface lightly with semi-skimmed milk and bake for an additional 3–4 minutes, then cool again.

title: Spiced Sweet Potato Pie with Oat Crust and Maple-Pecan Glaze
ingredients_json: ["600 g sweet potatoes, orange flesh, peeled", "200 g eggs, whole", "150 g Greek yogurt, plain, low-fat", "60 g maple syrup", "80 g rolled oats", "40 g almonds, ground", "70 g unsalted butter", "5 g ground cinnamon", "2 g ground ginger", "2 g ground nutmeg", "2 g fine salt", "5 ml vanilla extract", "30 g pecans, chopped"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Cook the peeled sweet potatoes in lightly salted water until very soft, about 20 minutes, then drain well and mash until smooth. In a bowl, mix the mashed sweet potatoes with the eggs, Greek yogurt, maple syrup, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, vanilla extract, and fine salt until fully combined and silky. For the crust, pulse the oats and ground almonds together, then rub in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Press the oat crumb mixture into a 22–24 cm pie dish and bake for 10 minutes to set. Remove from the oven, sprinkle over the chopped pecans, and pour in the sweet potato filling. Bake for 35–45 minutes, until the center is just set with a slight wobble and the edges are lightly browned. Let the pie cool to room temperature before slicing, so the filling fully firms up.

title: Warm Spiced Sweet Potato Pie with Oat Crust and Vanilla
ingredients_json: ["450 g sweet potato, raw", "120 g rolled oats", "60 g walnuts, chopped", "50 g unsalted butter", "1 piece egg, raw", "120 g Greek yogurt, plain 2%", "80 g brown sugar", "120 ml milk, low-fat", "2 tsp ground cinnamon", "1 tsp ground ginger", "0.25 tsp ground nutmeg", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "2 g salt", "1 tbsp lemon juice"]
instructions:
Preheat your oven to 180°C. Peel and dice the sweet potatoes, then steam or boil them until very tender, about 15–18 minutes; drain well. Add the warm sweet potatoes to a blender or bowl and mash until smooth. Stir in the milk, Greek yogurt, egg, brown sugar, vanilla extract, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, lemon juice, and salt until the filling looks silky and fully combined.

To make the crust, pulse the oats and walnuts until they resemble coarse crumbs, then mix with the melted butter until the mixture holds together when pressed. Press the crust firmly into the base and slightly up the sides of a 20–22 cm pie dish. Pour the sweet potato filling into the crust.

Bake for 35–45 minutes, until the edges are set and the center is just slightly wobbly when you gently shake the pan. Let the pie cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing so it firms up. For best flavor, serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Spiced Baked Sweet Potato Pie with Cinnamon-Oat Crust
ingredients_json: ["450 g sweet potatoes, raw", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, low-fat", "100 g light brown sugar", "2 piece eggs, whole, raw", "30 g butter, unsalted", "10 g ground cinnamon", "2 g ground ginger", "1 g ground nutmeg", "2 g salt, table", "60 g rolled oats", "40 g whole wheat flour", "50 g milk, skimmed", "5 g vanilla extract", "8 g baking powder", "30 g raisins"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C. Peel the sweet potatoes, cut them into small cubes, and steam or boil them until very tender, about 15–18 minutes. Drain well and mash until smooth. In a bowl, mix the oats, whole wheat flour, baking powder, and 1 g salt. Melt the butter and stir it together with the milk and vanilla, then combine with the dry ingredients until you get a crumbly, cohesive crust. Press the crust mixture into the bottom and a little up the sides of a greased 20–22 cm pie dish. In a separate bowl, beat the eggs with the brown sugar until glossy, then whisk in the Greek yogurt, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and the remaining salt. Fold in the mashed sweet potato and the raisins. Pour the filling into the crust and smooth the top. Bake for 35–45 minutes, until the edges are set and the center has a slight wobble when you gently shake the pan. Let the pie cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour before slicing for clean pieces.

title: Classic Sweet Potato Pie with Cinnamon-Pecan Oat Crust
ingredients_json: ["600 g sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed", "200 g low-fat Greek yogurt", "2 piece eggs, whole, raw", "90 g honey", "60 g rolled oats", "50 g pecans", "80 g unsalted butter, melted", "20 g brown sugar", "10 g ground cinnamon", "2 g ground ginger", "3 g fine salt", "5 ml vanilla extract", "30 ml milk, low-fat"]
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a 23 cm pie dish. In a food processor, pulse the rolled oats and pecans until they resemble coarse crumbs, then stir in the melted butter and brown sugar until evenly moistened. Press the mixture firmly into the bottom and a little up the sides of the pie dish, then bake for 10 minutes until set. Meanwhile, boil or steam the sweet potato cubes until very tender, about 20 minutes, then drain well and mash until smooth. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, honey, Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, cinnamon, ginger, salt, and milk until glossy. Fold the mashed sweet potatoes into the filling and mix until completely smooth. Pour the filling into the crust and bake for 35–45 minutes, until the edges look set and the center still jiggles slightly when you gently shake the pan. Let the pie cool to room temperature, then chill for at least 2 hours before slicing for clean portions.

title: Light Greek Yogurt Tiramisu with Espresso and Cocoa
ingredients_json: ["250 g mascarpone, reduced-fat", "300 g Greek yogurt, low-fat 2%", "60 g erythritol", "2 tsp vanilla extract", "250 ml espresso coffee, strong, cooled", "60 ml coffee liqueur, optional", "24 g instant coffee powder", "250 g savoiardi biscuits (ladyfingers)", "1 g ground cinnamon", "10 g unsweetened cocoa powder, Dutch-process"]
instructions: Brew 250 ml strong espresso (or make it from instant coffee), then cool it completely. In a bowl, whisk the reduced-fat mascarpone with the low-fat Greek yogurt, erythritol, vanilla extract, and cinnamon until smooth and thick. If you’re using coffee liqueur, stir it into the cooled espresso for extra depth. Quickly dip the savoiardi biscuits into the espresso mixture for about 1–2 seconds per side so they absorb liquid without turning mushy, then arrange a first layer in a serving dish. Spread half of the mascarpone-yogurt mixture over the biscuits, add a second layer of dipped biscuits, then cover with the remaining mixture. Dust the top evenly with cocoa powder and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until set and sliceable.

title: Greek Yogurt Tiramisu Cups with Coffee and Cocoa
ingredients_json: ["500 g low-fat Greek yogurt, plain", "250 g mascarpone", "80 g powdered erythritol", "2 pcs eggs, raw", "2 tsp vanilla extract", "180 ml espresso coffee, cooled", "20 g cocoa powder, unsweetened", "200 g savoiardi biscuits (ladyfinger), whole wheat", "2 tbsp dark rum (optional)"]
instructions: Brew espresso and let it cool to room temperature. In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the erythritol until the mixture looks lighter and thicker. Stir in the mascarpone and vanilla extract until smooth, then fold in the Greek yogurt gently so the texture stays airy. In a clean bowl, whisk the egg whites until they form soft peaks and fold them into the mascarpone-yogurt mixture. Mix the cooled coffee with the rum if using. Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the coffee, about 1–2 seconds per side so they do not fall apart, then layer them into serving cups. Spread half of the cream over the biscuits, add another layer of dipped biscuits, and finish with the remaining cream. Sift cocoa powder over the top. Chill the tiramisu cups in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, so the biscuits soften and the flavors meld.

title: Greek Yogurt Tiramisu with Cocoa and Coffee-Soaked Savoiardi
ingredients_json: ["250 g Greek yogurt, nonfat", "250 g mascarpone", "80 g honey", "2 piece eggs, raw", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "300 ml espresso, hot", "200 g Savoiardi biscuits (ladyfingers)", "35 g cocoa powder, unsweetened", "20 ml amaretto"]
instructions: Brew a strong espresso and keep it hot. In a bowl, separate the eggs and whisk the egg yolks with the honey and vanilla extract until the mixture looks slightly lighter. Add the mascarpone and Greek yogurt and mix until smooth and creamy. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg whites until they hold soft peaks, then gently fold them into the mascarpone mixture so you keep the airiness. Combine the hot espresso with the amaretto. Quickly dip the ladyfingers in the coffee mixture for about 1–2 seconds each side so they soak but don’t turn to mush, then arrange a layer in a serving dish. Spread half the cream over the biscuits, add another layer of coffee-dipped ladyfingers, and finish with the remaining cream. Dust generously with cocoa powder. Chill for at least 4 hours before serving so the layers set and the flavor fully develops.

title: Salted Date-Caramel Toffee Squares with Toasted Oats
ingredients_json: ["180 g dates, pitted", "120 g rolled oats", "60 ml unsweetened almond milk", "40 g peanut butter, natural", "20 g coconut oil, refined", "1 g fine salt", "5 ml vanilla extract", "30 g dark chocolate, 70% cacao"]
instructions: Toast the rolled oats in a dry nonstick pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until they smell nutty and lightly golden. Soak the pitted dates in the almond milk for 5 minutes, then blend to a smooth caramel paste. In the same pan, melt the coconut oil and stir in the date caramel and peanut butter over low heat until glossy and thick, about 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from the heat and fold in the toasted oats and vanilla, then spread the mixture into a parchment-lined small tray (about 20x20 cm) and press firmly with a spatula. Melt the dark chocolate gently and drizzle or spread a thin layer over the top, then sprinkle the remaining salt lightly if desired. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours until set, cut into squares, and serve cold or let sit 5 minutes for a softer toffee bite.

title: Light Salted Date Toffee with Toasted Oats and Coconut
ingredients_json: ["120 g pitted dates, Medjool", "60 g rolled oats", "40 g coconut cream", "30 g almond butter", "20 g coconut flakes, unsweetened", "1.5 g sea salt", "1 g vanilla extract"]
instructions: Toast the rolled oats in a dry non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until they smell nutty and lightly golden. Let them cool for 2 minutes. Meanwhile, blend the dates with coconut cream and vanilla extract until you get a smooth, thick paste. Stir the toasted oats, almond butter, coconut flakes, and sea salt into the date mixture until evenly combined. Spread the mixture into a parchment-lined small dish and press firmly to remove air pockets. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, then cut into portions and serve cold for a chewy toffee-like bite.

title: Salted Date-Toffee Squares with Almond Butter and Sea Salt
ingredients_json: ["200 g pitted dates, Medjool", "60 g almond butter", "30 g coconut oil, refined", "50 g Greek yogurt, 2%", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "1 g sea salt", "40 g oats, rolled"]
instructions: Line a small baking pan (about 20 x 20 cm) with baking paper. In a saucepan over low heat, warm the dates with the coconut oil for 3–4 minutes until they soften and look glossy. Transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until smooth. Stir in the almond butter, Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, and sea salt, then mix until thick and fully combined. Fold in the oats and spread the mixture evenly into the prepared pan. Chill for at least 2 hours, until set firmly. Cut into squares and serve chilled for the cleanest toffee texture.

title: Light Salted Caramel Oat Toffee Squares with Yogurt Crunch
ingredients_json: ["120 g rolled oats", "80 g pitted dates, chopped", "60 g unsalted butter", "2 tbsp light brown sugar", "120 ml low-fat yogurt, plain", "1 tsp sea salt", "1 tsp vanilla extract"]
instructions: Toast the rolled oats in a dry saucepan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until they smell nutty and look slightly golden. Add the chopped dates and butter, then cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, stirring until the mixture becomes thick and glossy. Remove from the heat and stir in the brown sugar, sea salt, and vanilla extract. Press the toffee mixture firmly into a parchment-lined small tray (about 20 x 20 cm) and chill for 20 minutes. Mix the plain low-fat yogurt until smooth, then spread it evenly over the chilled toffee. Chill for another 30 minutes until set, then slice into squares and serve cold.

title: Light Salted Oat Caramel Toffee Squares
ingredients_json: ["120 g rolled oats", "60 g almond butter", "80 g honey", "30 g unsalted butter", "1 g fine sea salt", "60 g dark chocolate 70% cacao", "40 g unsweetened applesauce"]
instructions: Toast the rolled oats in a dry non-stick saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring constantly, until they smell nutty and lightly golden. Reduce the heat to low and add the almond butter, honey, and unsalted butter. Stir until the mixture turns glossy and smooth, then whisk in the applesauce and sea salt. Continue cooking on low for 2 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pan to prevent sticking. Pour the warm caramel onto a parchment-lined small tray (about 20×20 cm) and spread it into an even layer, then let it cool for 20 minutes until set. Melt the dark chocolate gently in a microwave in 20-second bursts or over a very low heat, then drizzle or spread it over the toffee layer. Sprinkle lightly with a final touch of salt if desired, then chill for 30–45 minutes until the chocolate firms. Cut into squares and serve chilled or at cool room temperature.

title: Light Raspberry Greek Yogurt Torte with Almond-Oat Base
ingredients_json: ["140 g Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "200 g Greek yogurt, 0% fat", "130 g raspberries, fresh", "80 g rolled oats", "40 g almonds, ground", "60 g honey", "200 ml oat milk, unsweetened", "30 g chia seeds", "10 g lemon juice", "4 g vanilla extract", "6 g gelatin powder", "1 g salt", "1 g lemon zest"]
instructions: Line a 20–22 cm springform tin with baking paper and lightly grease the sides. In a bowl, mix the oats, ground almonds, 1 g salt, and half of the honey, then press firmly into the base. Chill the tin while you prepare the filling. Warm the oat milk gently (do not boil) and whisk in the gelatin until fully dissolved. In a separate bowl, mix the Greek yogurt (both kinds) with the remaining honey, lemon juice, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Pour the warm gelatin mixture into the yogurt mixture while stirring, then fold in about half of the raspberries. Pour the filling over the chilled base, spread smooth, and scatter the remaining raspberries on top. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until set and sliceable. Serve cold, with any extra raspberries if you like.

title: Light Berry Yogurt Torte with Greek Yogurt and Oats
ingredients_json: ["200 g Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "250 g mixed berries, fresh or frozen", "120 g oats", "60 g almonds, ground", "80 g honey", "2 pieces egg, raw", "10 g lemon juice", "1 g vanilla extract", "6 g baking powder", "1 g fine salt", "30 ml olive oil"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 170°C and lightly grease a 20–22 cm springform pan. In a bowl, mix the oats, ground almonds, baking powder, and salt. In a second bowl, whisk the eggs with the honey until glossy, then whisk in the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, vanilla extract, and olive oil. Fold the dry oat mixture into the yogurt mixture until you have a thick batter. Spoon half the batter into the pan, scatter half the berries over, then cover with the remaining batter and finish with the rest of the berries on top. Bake for 28–35 minutes, until the torte is set in the center and lightly golden; it should spring back when gently pressed. Let it cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then release the sides and cool fully before slicing so it holds together.

title: Greek Yogurt Berry Torte with Chia-Oat Crust (No-Bake)
ingredients_json: ["200 g Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "250 g cottage cheese, low-fat", "80 g honey", "200 g mixed berries, fresh or frozen", "30 g chia seeds", "80 g rolled oats", "60 g almonds, ground", "2 tsp vanilla extract", "1 tbsp lemon juice", "5 g lemon zest", "70 g coconut oil, refined", "1 pinch sea salt"]
instructions: Mix the rolled oats and ground almonds with the chia seeds. Melt the coconut oil and stir it into the oat mixture along with the lemon zest and a pinch of sea salt until evenly combined. Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of a 20–22 cm springform pan and refrigerate for 30 minutes to set. In a bowl, blend the Greek yogurt and cottage cheese until smooth, then stir in the honey and vanilla extract. Gently fold in half of the berries. Spread the yogurt filling over the crust, smooth the top, and scatter the remaining berries on top. Chill the torte for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until set. Slice with a warm knife and serve cold.

title: Light Berry Greek Yogurt Torte with Almond-Oat Crust
ingredients_json: ["180 g rolled oats", "60 g almonds, ground", "40 g unsalted butter", "1 tbsp honey", "1 pinch fine salt", "500 g Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "200 g mixed berries, fresh or frozen", "30 g chia seeds", "40 g maple syrup", "2 tsp vanilla extract", "6 g gelatin powder", "30 ml cold water", "1 tbsp lemon juice"]
instructions: Grind the rolled oats finely, then mix with the ground almonds and a pinch of fine salt. Melt the butter and stir in the honey, then combine with the oat-almond mixture to form a crumbly, pressable base. Press the crust firmly into the bottom of a 20–22 cm springform pan and chill while you prepare the filling. In a bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt with maple syrup, vanilla extract, and lemon juice. Sprinkle the gelatin powder over the cold water and let it bloom for 5 minutes, then gently heat it until just dissolved and smooth (do not boil). Stir the dissolved gelatin into the yogurt mixture, then fold in the chia seeds and the berries. Pour the filling over the chilled crust, smooth the top, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set. Slice with a warm knife and serve cold.

title: Cocoa Oat Truffles with Greek Yogurt and Almonds
ingredients_json: ["200 g dark chocolate, 70% cocoa, chopped", "120 g plain Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "60 g rolled oats, finely ground", "30 g almonds, ground", "20 ml honey", "10 ml vanilla extract", "20 g cocoa powder, unsweetened", "2 g fine salt"]
instructions: Gently melt the chopped dark chocolate using a microwave in short bursts of 20 seconds or over a very low heat in a bowl set above barely simmering water. Stir until smooth and glossy, then let it cool for about 5 minutes so it is warm but not hot. Stir the Greek yogurt, honey, and vanilla extract into the melted chocolate, then fold in the ground oats and ground almonds until a thick, scoopable truffle mixture forms. Cover and chill the mixture in the refrigerator for 60 minutes, until firm enough to roll. Scoop and roll into small balls (about 18–22 g each). Roll the truffles in unsweetened cocoa powder, then chill again for 15 minutes before serving. Store covered in the refrigerator and serve slightly chilled for the best texture.

title: Dark Chocolate Cocoa-Mint Greek Yogurt Truffles
ingredients_json: ["200 g dark chocolate, 70% cacao, chopped", "150 g Greek yogurt, plain, low-fat", "30 g cocoa powder, unsweetened", "15 ml honey", "20 g almond flour", "5 g butter, unsalted", "1 g peppermint extract", "2 g flaky sea salt"]
instructions: Melt the dark chocolate with the butter using a low heat setting in a small bowl over a pot of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat and let the chocolate mixture cool for about 5 minutes so it is no longer hot. Stir in the Greek yogurt, honey, cocoa powder, almond flour, peppermint extract, and flaky sea salt until you have a thick, glossy truffle mixture. Cover and refrigerate for 45 minutes, until firm enough to scoop. Scoop about 1 tablespoon portions, roll quickly between your palms, and place the truffles on a plate lined with baking paper. Chill again for at least 30 minutes before serving so they hold their shape.

title: Dark Chocolate Berry Oat Truffles with Greek Yogurt
ingredients_json: ["180 g dark chocolate, 70% cocoa, chopped", "120 g Greek yogurt, plain, 2%", "40 g rolled oats", "60 g frozen raspberries", "20 g honey", "10 g unsweetened cocoa powder", "2 g vanilla extract"]
instructions: Warm the Greek yogurt gently in a small saucepan over low heat until it is just steaming, then remove from the heat. Add the chopped dark chocolate and stir until completely melted and glossy. Pulse the rolled oats into a coarse oat meal, then stir them into the chocolate mixture. Thaw the raspberries slightly, then mash them well and fold into the truffle mixture. Stir in the honey, cocoa powder, and vanilla extract, mixing until smooth. Cover and chill the mixture for 2 hours, until firm enough to scoop. Scoop out 18 portions and roll quickly into balls with cold hands, then coat lightly with a little extra cocoa powder if desired. Serve chilled for a firmer texture, or let sit at room temperature for 5–10 minutes for a softer center.

title: Cacao-Chia Date Truffles with Orange Zest (No-Bake)
ingredients_json: ["120 g Medjool dates, pitted", "60 g dark chocolate, 70% cocoa", "120 g plain Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "20 g chia seeds, whole", "25 g cocoa powder, unsweetened", "10 ml orange juice", "1 g orange zest", "2 g vanilla extract", "1 g fine salt"]
instructions: Finely chop the dates and blend them with the orange juice until you get a thick paste. Melt the dark chocolate gently (either in short microwave bursts or over a very low heat) until smooth, then let it cool for 5 minutes so it doesn’t seize the yogurt. In a bowl, stir the Greek yogurt, chia seeds, melted chocolate, vanilla extract, orange zest, and salt into the date paste. Cover and refrigerate for 60 minutes so the chia can thicken the mixture. Scoop out portions and roll them quickly between your hands to form truffles, then roll each truffle in the unsweetened cocoa powder. Serve straight away or keep refrigerated for up to 3 days; the truffles should feel firm but slightly soft in the center.

title: Cocoa-Oat Date Truffles with Toasted Hazelnuts
ingredients_json: ["200 g dark chocolate 70% (chopped)", "250 g Medjool dates (pitted)", "120 ml unsweetened almond milk", "30 g cocoa powder", "60 g rolled oats", "80 g hazelnuts", "10 g coconut oil (melted)", "5 g flaky sea salt"]
instructions: Pulse the hazelnuts and rolled oats separately until they resemble coarse crumbs, then set aside. Soak the pitted dates in the almond milk for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth into a thick paste. Melt the chopped dark chocolate with the coconut oil over low heat, stirring until glossy and fully melted; remove from the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes so it doesn’t seize the mixture. Fold the date paste into the chocolate, then mix in the cocoa powder, hazelnut-oat crumbs, and flaky sea salt until everything is evenly combined. Chill the mixture for 45 minutes until it is firm enough to scoop. Scoop and roll into small truffles (about 18–20 g each). For a neat finish, roll the truffles in extra cocoa powder if desired, then chill another 15 minutes before serving.

title: Blueberry Greek Yogurt Upside-Down Cakes with Cinnamon
ingredients_json: ["250 g blueberries, fresh", "60 g brown sugar", "40 g unsalted butter", "2 piece eggs, whole", "200 g Greek yogurt, low-fat plain", "120 g wheat flour, whole wheat", "30 g oats, rolled", "10 g baking powder", "5 g ground cinnamon", "2 g salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Grease four small baking molds and line a baking tray for stability. In a small saucepan, melt the butter and stir in the brown sugar until it looks like a smooth caramel. Spoon a little caramel into the bottom of each mold, then scatter blueberries evenly over the caramel. In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the Greek yogurt until glossy. Stir in the whole wheat flour, oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt, mixing just until no dry flour remains. Divide the batter between the molds and spread it gently to the edges. Bake for 20–24 minutes, until the tops are lightly golden and a toothpick comes out mostly clean. Let the cakes cool for 10 minutes, then carefully invert onto plates so the blueberries sit on top. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Pineapple Coconut Upside-Down Oat Cakes
ingredients_json: ["20 g almond flour", "60 g rolled oats", "1 tsp baking powder", "1 g ground cinnamon", "1 g fine salt", "120 g nonfat Greek yogurt", "2 piece eggs, whole", "70 g maple syrup", "60 g unsweetened applesauce", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "120 g canned pineapple rings, drained", "15 g shredded unsweetened coconut", "15 g olive oil, extra-virgin"]
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C. Drain the pineapple rings well and pat them dry. Lightly grease a muffin tin or small cake pan. Place pineapple rings in the bottom of each cavity and sprinkle a little shredded coconut over them. In a bowl, blend the eggs, Greek yogurt, maple syrup, applesauce, vanilla extract, and olive oil until smooth. Stir in the rolled oats, almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt, then let the batter sit for 5 minutes so it thickens. Pour the batter over the pineapple so it almost covers the fruit. Bake for 18–22 minutes until the tops are golden and a toothpick in the cake portion (not touching the pineapple) comes out clean. Let the cakes cool for 10 minutes, then run a thin knife around the edges and invert onto a plate so the pineapple sits on top. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Apple Cinnamon Upside-Down Oat Cakes with Greek Yogurt
ingredients_json: ["500 g apples, firm, cored and sliced", "60 g rolled oats", "120 g plain Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "2 piece eggs, raw", "40 g honey", "30 g whole wheat flour", "60 ml rapeseed oil", "1 tsp baking powder", "1 tsp ground cinnamon", "0.5 g fine salt", "10 g butter, salted (for the pan)"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C and grease a 20 cm round cake tin with the butter. Sprinkle half of the sliced apples into the bottom, then arrange the rest on top so they cover the surface. Drizzle over half of the honey and dust lightly with cinnamon. Blend the rolled oats into a fine oat flour. In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the remaining honey, then mix in the Greek yogurt and rapeseed oil until smooth. Stir in the oat flour, whole wheat flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and the salt, and mix just until you have a thick batter. Spoon the batter over the apples and spread it gently to the edges. Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the top is golden and a skewer inserted into the cake part comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then invert carefully onto a serving plate. Serve warm for the most tender apple layer.

title: Blueberry & Greek Yogurt Upside-Down Cakes with Vanilla Oats
ingredients_json: ["250 g blueberries, fresh or frozen", "60 g honey", "30 g unsalted butter", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, low-fat", "2 piece egg", "120 g rolled oats", "120 ml milk, semi-skimmed", "2 tsp vanilla extract", "10 g baking powder", "1 g salt", "1 tbsp lemon juice"]
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a muffin tin with 6–8 paper liners. In a small saucepan, melt the butter with half of the honey over low heat, then stir in the blueberries and lemon juice. Cook for 4 minutes until the berries soften and release some juice, then divide the berry mixture evenly among the muffin wells. Blend the rolled oats into a fine flour, then whisk with baking powder and salt in a bowl. In another bowl, mix Greek yogurt, eggs, the remaining honey, vanilla extract, and milk until smooth, then fold into the dry ingredients to form a thick batter. Spoon the batter over the blueberries, filling each well about three-quarters full. Bake for 18–22 minutes until the tops are set and a toothpick comes out clean. Let the cakes cool for 10 minutes, then carefully turn them out onto a plate so the blueberries sit on top. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Skillet Berry Yogurt Upside-Down Cakes with Vanilla Oats
ingredients_json: ["180 g mixed berries, fresh or frozen", "30 g rolled oats", "120 g plain Greek yogurt, 2%", "2 piece eggs, whole", "80 g light brown sugar", "30 g unsalted butter", "1 tsp baking powder", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "1 pinch salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C. Melt the butter and lightly brush or grease a 20–22 cm oven-safe skillet or cake pan. Spread the mixed berries evenly over the bottom. In a bowl, blend the oats into a fine oat flour, then whisk eggs, Greek yogurt, brown sugar, vanilla extract, baking powder, and the salt until smooth. Pour the batter over the berries, making sure the berries are covered. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the top is golden and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then carefully invert onto a plate so the berries become the topping. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Whole-Wheat Chocolate Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Filling
ingredients_json: ["180 g whole-wheat flour", "30 g unsweetened cocoa powder", "8 g baking powder", "6 g baking soda", "2 g fine salt", "170 g natural cane sugar", "2 g ground cinnamon", "2 large eggs", "120 ml buttermilk", "80 ml sunflower oil", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "220 g plain low-fat Greek yogurt", "40 g honey", "40 g dark chocolate chips", "5 g cornstarch"]
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C and line two baking trays with baking paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and cane sugar until no lumps remain. In another bowl, whisk the eggs, buttermilk, sunflower oil, and vanilla extract. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until a thick, scoopable batter forms. Fold in the dark chocolate chips, then portion 18 small mounds onto the trays, leaving space between them. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the tops spring back lightly when touched and the edges look set. Let the pies cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. For the filling, whisk the Greek yogurt, honey, and cornstarch until smooth and glossy. Pipe or spread a generous amount of filling onto the flat side of half the pies, then sandwich with the remaining pies. Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving to firm up the filling.

title: Cocoa-Buckwheat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Vanilla Filling
ingredients_json: ["150 g wholemeal wheat flour", "90 g buckwheat flour", "30 g unsweetened cocoa powder", "10 g baking powder", "6 g baking soda", "2 g fine salt", "150 g Greek yogurt, nonfat", "120 g egg, whole", "140 g honey", "80 ml rapeseed oil", "1 tbsp vanilla extract", "250 g Greek yogurt, nonfat", "120 g powdered erythritol", "300 g mixed berries, frozen"]
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays with baking paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the wholemeal wheat flour, buckwheat flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and fine salt until the mixture looks evenly dark. In a second bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt, whole eggs, honey, rapeseed oil, and vanilla extract until smooth. Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix just until you have a thick, spoonable batter. Scoop 16 small rounds (about 30–35 g each) onto the trays, leaving space between them, and bake for 10–12 minutes until the tops spring back when lightly pressed. Let the cookies cool completely on the tray. Meanwhile, make the filling by mixing the nonfat Greek yogurt with powdered erythritol and stirring until smooth. Thaw the frozen mixed berries and mash them slightly, then fold in 60 g of the berry mixture into the yogurt for a lightly fruity filling. Spread about 1–1.5 tablespoons of filling on the flat side of half the whoopie pies, add a small spoonful of remaining mashed berries on top, and sandwich with the remaining pies. Chill for 15 minutes so the filling sets before serving.

title: Cocoa Oat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Vanilla Filling
ingredients_json: ["170 g wholemeal wheat flour", "80 g rolled oats, finely ground", "35 g unsweetened cocoa powder", "8 g baking powder", "3 g bicarbonate of soda", "4 g fine salt", "180 g light brown sugar", "2 piece eggs, whole, raw", "120 ml buttermilk", "80 ml rapeseed oil", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "250 g plain Greek yogurt, 2%", "120 g icing sugar", "10 g butter, unsalted", "1 tsp vanilla extract", "30 g dark chocolate chips"]
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays with baking paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the wholemeal flour, ground oats, cocoa powder, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, and salt. In another bowl, whisk the brown sugar, eggs, buttermilk, rapeseed oil, and vanilla extract until smooth, then pour into the dry ingredients and mix just until a thick, spoonable batter forms. Spoon about 2 tablespoons of batter onto the trays, leaving space for spreading, and bake for 9–11 minutes until the tops spring back lightly and the edges look set. Let the pies cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. For the filling, beat the Greek yogurt with icing sugar, melted butter, and vanilla extract until creamy, then fold in the dark chocolate chips. Spread or pipe a generous amount of filling onto the flat side of half the pies, top with the remaining pies, and chill for 20–30 minutes so the filling sets before serving.

title: Cocoa-Oat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Filling
ingredients_json: ["180 g rolled oats, finely ground", "60 g wholemeal spelt flour", "30 g unsweetened cocoa powder", "10 g baking powder", "4 g baking soda", "120 g honey", "60 g coconut oil, melted", "2 large eggs", "240 ml low-fat buttermilk", "1 g fine salt", "250 g Greek yogurt, 2% fat", "80 g powdered erythritol", "5 ml vanilla extract", "20 g dark chocolate, 70% cocoa, finely chopped"]
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays with parchment paper. In a bowl, whisk together the ground oats, spelt flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. In a separate bowl, whisk the honey, melted coconut oil, and eggs until smooth, then stir in the buttermilk and vanilla. Combine the wet and dry ingredients and mix until you have a thick, scoopable batter; if it feels very stiff, let it rest for 3 minutes so the oats hydrate. Scoop 12–14 g portions onto the trays, leaving space between each, and bake for 10–12 minutes until the pies spring back when lightly pressed. Let them cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. For the filling, stir the Greek yogurt with powdered erythritol and vanilla until thick and creamy, then fold in the chopped dark chocolate. Match similarly sized cookies and spread or pipe the filling on the flat side of half the pies, then top with the remaining pies and gently press to seal.

title: Wholegrain Oat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Berry Filling
ingredients_json: ["180 g wholemeal wheat flour", "120 g rolled oats, ground into flour", "8 g baking powder", "4 g bicarbonate of soda", "3 g fine sea salt", "120 g light brown sugar", "120 g unsalted butter, softened", "2 piece egg, raw", "80 ml low-fat milk", "10 ml vanilla extract", "200 g plain low-fat Greek yogurt", "80 g icing sugar", "200 g mixed berries, fresh or frozen", "10 g lemon zest", "20 g cocoa powder, unsweetened"]
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays with baking paper. In a bowl, whisk together the wholemeal flour, oat flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, salt, and cocoa powder. In a second bowl, cream the softened butter with the light brown sugar until lighter in color. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla extract and milk. Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until you have a thick, scoopable batter. Spoon small rounds (about 25–30 g each) onto the trays, leaving space for spreading, and bake for 10–12 minutes until the edges look set and the tops spring back lightly when touched. Let the whoopie pie rounds cool completely. For the filling, mash the berries with the lemon zest and stir into the Greek yogurt. Sift and mix in the icing sugar until the filling is creamy but holds its shape. Spread or pipe a generous layer of berry-yogurt filling on the flat side of half the rounds, then sandwich with the remaining rounds and serve within a few hours for best texture.
